article_title: The Effect of Dynamic Web Technologies on Student Academic Achievement in Problem-Based Collaborative Learning Environment
citation: Agâh Tuğrul KORUCU, Hasan ÇAKIR. (2018). The Effect of Dynamic Web Technologies on Student Academic Achievement in Problem-Based Collaborative Learning Environment. Malaysian Online Journal of Educational Technology, Volume 6, Issue 1. https://www.mojet.net
title: Dynamic web technology-supported problem-based collaborative learning environment built on Google tools
description: An 8-week online collaborative environment for problem-based learning, developed with Nelson's (2009) collaborative problem solving method and expert input. It used "Google+ Circle, Google Chat, Google+ Documents, Mind 42 (for creating online concept maps), Google+, Blogger, Google Hangouts (for verbal, written and visual calls) Google+ Homepage (sharing the video records), Google Calendar, and Google+, Drive (Survey)". Experimental-group students saved weekly work in blogs and Google Drive while solving real designed problems.
requirements: Students need adequate technological knowledge and experience with the environment and the dynamic web technologies available, as the research group had received prior IT coursework
constraints: The environment was designed and evaluated with pre-service ICT teachers in a department with substantial computer laboratories and Internet infrastructure
target_learners: pre-service ICT teachers in teacher education
target_learning_goals: 21st century proficiencies such as communication and cooperation
examples: Experimental-group students saved their analysis, shared information, feedback, comments and evaluations in weekly blogs and Google Drive while solving real designed problems weekly
key_sources: Agâh Tuğrul KORUCU, Hasan ÇAKIR. (2018). The Effect of Dynamic Web Technologies on Student Academic Achievement in Problem-Based Collaborative Learning Environment. Malaysian Online Journal of Educational Technology, Volume 6, Issue 1. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1165485

article_title: A combined approach of simulation-based "debriefing with good judgment" and case-based learning to enhance clinical thinking in Chinese residents.
citation: Shao Wenming, Cheng Xin, Gu Wanjie, Yan Yu, Liu Hiu, Zhang Jialin, Zhang Li, Yin Haiyan, Zhang Mingya. (2025). A combined approach of simulation-based "debriefing with good judgment" and case-based learning to enhance clinical thinking in Chinese residents. Frontiers in Public Health. https://doi.org/10.3389/fpubh.2025.1718961
title: Simulation session structure pairing 20-minute hands-on CBL practice with a 20-minute DwGJ roundtable debriefing
description: A lesson-level simulation design in which resident subgroups of four rotate hands-on and observer roles during a case scenario, then debrief. The article specifies that "Each 20-min hands-on session was followed by a 20-min DwGJ roundtable debriefing", using the Plus/Delta strategy and Advocacy and Inquiry, with a hands-on member recounting the case evolution and the instructor facilitating analysis and offering solutions, at total teaching hours matched to conventional CBL.
requirements: SimMan 3G simulator and case scenarios at elementary, intermediate, and advanced complexity
An instructor facilitator to identify procedural variations and guide deeper analysis
constraints: The duration of some debriefing sessions was not strictly controlled, which occasionally limited the time available for trainees to practice specific technical skills
target_learners: first-year resident physicians across internal medicine, surgery, obstetrics and gynecology, pediatrics, emergency medicine, and intensive care medicine
examples: Control group participants practiced skills for 40 minutes with instructor supervision, while the DwGJ group practiced 20 minutes and debriefed 20 minutes on the same clinical cases

A combined approach of simulation-based "debriefing with good judgment" and case-based learning to enhance clinical thinking in Chinese residents.
